title: Dispatch TUR 5: The Letter After the Crash
summary: A guard’s last message changes the question facing Alderwick.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The letter addressed to “Whoever Is Waiting at Alderwick” was opened yesterday before Mr. Pike, Dr. Saye, and two independent witnesses. Guard Amos Pell reports that the bridge did not simply collapse. As the train crossed the marsh, the far bank vanished. He saw Alderwick’s signal lamps ahead, but no platform beneath them.

“We have travelled the whole road,” he writes. “There must be a place at which it ends.” Pell says the passengers remained in the carriages while water rose below the wheels. His final line asks the stationmaster to show a light. The railway has no stationmaster, and there were no signal lamps installed at its unbuilt terminus.

The Institute has since placed an experimental receiver in the coal cellar beneath the goods depot. Its needle moves when the 6:40 service would be in motion according to the old timetable. At other hours it remains still. Dr. Saye believes the train is approaching the proposed terminus along a route held in the Stratum by decades of plans, tickets, correspondence, and expectation.

Mr. Wren has offered to build a temporary platform against the cellar’s east wall. City officials have refused permission, citing the condition of the depot foundations. Mrs. Harrow brought her yellow umbrella to the cellar steps and stood there until dark. “If the letters can find us,” she said, “perhaps the children can.”

Alderman Felix Dorne has scheduled a public hearing. The city must decide whether attempting to receive a train that has not yet been built would draw its passengers out of danger—or open a passage that cannot be shut.
